title: Power Apps: Power Apps CLI commands to find connectors and create connections for code apps
summary: Hold: the data-policy navigation omits a documented Settings heading, and the environment automation entry describes an SDK property rather than a runnable update operation. The data-policy role guidance also extends an environment-level Dataverse qualification to tenant administrators. The roadmap details and the connector commands are supported; all cited Learn pages opened successfully in this check.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing, first paragraph
claims.claim: The change adds CLI commands for developers to discover connectors and create connections for code apps.
claims.quote: The Power Apps CLI adds new commands that let developers discover available connectors and create connections directly from the command line.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap describes wiring connectors without switching tools or manually configuring connections in the maker portal.
claims.quote: This enables developers to wire connectors into code apps as part of their normal development workflow, without switching tools or manually configuring connections in the maker portal.

claims.claim: The roadmap includes new agent.md files and how-to documentation for coding agents discovering connectors and creating connections.
claims.quote: New code app agent.md files and code app how-to documentation show how coding agents can handle connector discovery and connection creation as part of end-to-end prompt-to-app workflows.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is June CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "June CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap target date is July CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "July CY2026"

claims.where: What's changing, second paragraph; Governance guidance
claims.claim: pa connector list lists connectors available in the environment configured for the code app.
claims.quote: Use `pa connector list` command to find the connectors available in the Power Platform environment configured for your code app:

claims.claim: pa connector list supports --search and --json.
claims.quote: pa connector list [--search <term>] [--json]

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: pa connection create --connector <connector-id> creates a connection in the environment configured for the code app.
claims.quote:
Use `pa connection create` to create a connection in the environment configured for the code app:
pa connection create --connector <connector-id> [--display-name <name>] [--json]

claims.where: What's changing, second paragraph; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Successful connection creation returns the connection ID.
claims.quote: When the command succeeds, it returns the connection ID.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The returned connection ID is used to add the connector as an app data source.
claims.quote: Use the connection ID when you add the connector as a data source to the code app.

claims.claim: Connector discovery and connection creation run from an initialised code app project.
claims.quote:
Prerequisites
An initialized Power Apps code app.
Step 1: List available connectors
Run the commands in this article from the root of your code app project.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The GitHub Copilot CLI code apps plugin runs the CLI to scaffold, initialise, add connectors and implement the app after plan approval.
claims.quote:
When you approve the plan, the agent runs the code apps CLI to:
- Scaffold the project files
- Initialize the app
- Add connectors
- Implement functionality and UI, using the connectors
claims.fix: Call this the 'code apps preview plugin' in its first mention: the quickstart says 'Then install the code apps preview plugin'. This qualification concerns the agent plugin, not the release status of every connector command.

claims.where: What's changing, last paragraph; Open questions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the roadmap's agent.md files.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps code apps CLI agent.md files coding agents guidance. Opened code apps overview, CLI quickstart, connection how-to, connect-to-data and GitHub Copilot quickstart; no description of the roadmap's agent.md files found.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Adding the connection means the app can read or write whatever data that connector reaches.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps code apps data permissions connection. Opened connect-to-data and overview. They document adding data sources and calling generated services, not unrestricted access to whatever data a connector can reach.
claims.fix: Replace both versions of the broad access assertion with 'After adding a connection as a data source, the app can call the generated services for that data source.' See https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/code-apps/how-to/connect-to-data.

claims.claim: The Enable code apps path is Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Power Apps code apps > Enable code apps.
claims.quote: Go to Manage > Environments > select the environment where you use code apps. Go to Settings > Expand the Product subsection > Select Features. Go to the feature Power Apps code apps and use the Enable code apps toggle to turn it on.

claims.claim: Setting a bool PowerAppsAllowCodeApps property on an EnvironmentManagementSetting object is the documented automation operation for enabling code apps.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerAppsAllowCodeApps update environment settings Power Platform API PowerShell CLI. Opened the cited property reference, environment-management API create/update references and tutorial; the property page shows bool? get/set, not a setting-update operation.
claims.fix: Remove the non-runnable automation entry and its rendered call. Preserve only this informational note: 'The .NET SDK exposes nullable Boolean PowerAppsAllowCodeApps on EnvironmentManagementSetting; the property reference does not give a runnable update operation.' Do not describe the property assignment as persisting an environment setting or infer a request body from its name.

claims.claim: Power Platform admins and environment admins can set the environment option for code apps.
claims.quote: Admins can enable code apps by setting an environment option. Power Platform admins and environment admins can set this option.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Environment groups and rules can configure the code apps setting for multiple environments.
claims.quote: For management at scale, you can configure this setting for multiple environments at once by using environment groups and rules.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Enable code apps has a documented default of Off.
claims.quote:
| Setting | Description | Default value |
| Enable code apps | Allow users to bring apps they created outside of Power Apps and run them in Power Apps. If this setting is turned off, those apps don't run. | Off |

claims.claim: Code apps do not run in an environment when Enable code apps is turned off.
claims.quote: If this setting is turned off, those apps don't run.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: There is no documented separate admin switch or new mandatory admin action specific to these connector CLI commands.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps code apps CLI connector commands admin disable switch data policy connection create blocked connector. Opened overview, feature settings, connection how-to and CLI reference; no separate command switch or mandatory new admin action found.

claims.claim: The new optional CLI capability is user-opt-in, rather than a change that runs without a maker choosing to use it.
claims.quote: Use the Power Apps CLI to find connectors and create a connection without leaving your terminal or opening Power Apps.

claims.claim: The documented data-policy path is Security > Data and privacy > Data policy.
claims.quote: Select Security in the navigation pane. In the Security pane, under Settings, select Data and privacy. In the Data protection and privacy screen, select the Data policy section.
claims.fix: Replace the path in front matter and the rendered table with 'Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy'. The cited page explicitly includes the Settings group heading.

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy -DisplayName <name> -EnvironmentType <type> creates a data policy through Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell.
claims.quote:
Module: Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell Module
New-DlpPolicy -DisplayName <String> -EnvironmentType <String>
The New-DlpPolicy cmdlet creates a new DLP policy for the logged in admin's tenant.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate licence or meter for the connector CLI commands is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps code apps CLI licensing connector commands pricing limits premium connectors; code apps licensing Premium. Opened roadmap record, CLI reference, connection how-to, overview and Power Apps licensing FAQs; no command-specific licence or meter found.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Code-app end users need Power Apps Premium, pay-as-you-go enabled, an App Pass or auto-claim enabled.
claims.quote:
End users that run code apps need one of the following:
- Power Apps Premium license
- Pay-as-you-go enabled
- An App Pass
- Auto-claim enabled.

claims.claim: Auto-claim automatically assigns an available tenant premium licence to the user.
claims.quote: Auto-claim enabled. This option automatically assigns a premium license to the user if one is available in the tenant.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, reflecting the documented code-app licence and pay-as-you-go alternatives.
claims.quote:
End users that run code apps need one of the following:
- Power Apps Premium license
- Pay-as-you-go enabled

claims.claim: The data-policy page's Class attribute identifies whether a connector requires Premium licensing or is included in Built-in/Standard licensing.
claims.quote: Class | Indicates whether connector usage requires a Premium license or is it included in the Built-in/Standard license for Power Platform.

claims.claim: Which connectors are wired into a code app therefore affects its end-user licensing requirements.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps code apps CLI licensing connector commands pricing limits premium connectors; code apps licensing Premium. Opened overview, create-dlp-policy and licensing FAQs; none states a connector-dependent change to the code-app licensing routes already listed.
claims.fix: Remove 'Which connectors developers wire in therefore affects licensing'. Keep the documented Class attribute and the code-app licensing routes as separate facts; do not infer an additional or different code-app licence from connector class.

claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps code apps CLI connector connection commands preview generally available admin approval; code apps preview connection. Read CLI connector/connection reference sections, create-connection and connect-to-data; no per-command release-phase assignment found.

claims.claim: Connectors administrators do not want used can be placed in the Blocked data-policy group.

claims.fix: Replace the checklist bullet with 'Review the data policies that cover those environments, and confirm unwanted blockable connectors are in the Blocked group.' The qualification is necessary because not every connector can be blocked.

claims.claim: Creating, editing or deleting data policies requires Environment Admin or Power Platform admin permissions, replaced by System Administrator for any environment with Dataverse.
claims.quote:
Environment-level policies
To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions. For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.
claims.fix: Replace the role sentence with 'Tenant-level policies require the Power Platform Administrator role. Environment-level policies require Power Apps Environment Admin permissions, or the System Administrator role for environments with a Dataverse database.'
